title: Giants Eye Five QB Trades After Jaxson Dart’s Season-Ending Injury, Including Two Linked to John Harbaugh
body:
The New York Giants’ quarterback carousel has already spun twice this season, and a third rotation may be on the horizon. After Jaxson Dart’s season‑ending knee injury in the opening drive against the Dallas Cowboys, the Giants have been forced to rely on veteran Jameis Winston, whose performance has been a mixed bag. With the team’s offense sputtering and the NFC East race already slipping out of reach, New York’s front office is reportedly scouting a handful of mobile quarterbacks who could be acquired via trade before the deadline, two of whom have connections to Baltimore Ravens head coach John Harbaugh.

The first name circulating is Denver’s former first‑round pick, Bo Nix. Though he never cemented a starting role in Denver, Nix’s dual‑threat skill set—mobility, a strong arm, and a reputation for quick decision‑making—mirrors the profile the Giants have been chasing since the draft. Denver, meanwhile, is deep at quarterback with Drew Locke and a promising rookie in Sam Harris, making Nix a viable trade chip. A mid‑season swap would give New York a fresh arm that could better exploit the Giants’ revamped receiving corps, while Denver would acquire additional draft capital to continue building around its young defensive core.

A second prospect is Seattle’s veteran backup, Geno Smith. Smith’s resurgence with the Seahawks last season—highlighted by a 4.5 QBR and a clutch performance in the playoffs—has reignited interest from teams seeking a seasoned, yet still mobile, play‑maker. Seattle, sitting comfortably atop the AFC West, could entertain a deal that includes a late‑round pick and a conditional draft selection, especially if the Giants can sweeten the offer with a future fourth‑rounder. Smith’s experience in high‑pressure games would provide a steadier presence than Winston, whose turnover rate has risen to a concerning 2.1 per game.

The third candidate ties directly to Harbaugh’s network: Baltimore’s backup, Tyler Boyd. Though Boyd has spent most of his career as a practice‑squad player, he was a former fifth‑round pick who showed flashes of athleticism during limited snaps in 2023. Harbaugh’s familiarity with Boyd’s work ethic and developmental trajectory could make a trade feasible, especially if the Ravens are looking to offload a backup in exchange for a modest draft pick and a future defensive lineman. For the Giants, Boyd would represent a low‑risk, high‑upside gamble—he could be groomed as a short‑term starter while the team continues to evaluate its longer‑term options.

A fourth option is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ backup, Kyle Trask. Trask’s tenure as Tom Brady’s understudy gave him exposure to a sophisticated offense and a deep understanding of pocket passing, but he also displayed enough athleticism to extend plays when needed. Tampa Bay, now rebuilding after Brady’s retirement, may be willing to part with Trask for a conditional pick, especially if they can recoup a veteran presence on the defensive side. Trask could provide the Giants with a more traditional pocket passer to complement their deep‑route receivers, offering a contrast to Winston’s improvisational style.

Lastly, the Giants have not ruled out a bold move for the Indianapolis Colts’ rookie sensation, Michael Pennington. Pennington, a second‑round pick out of Ohio State, has already shown a knack for making plays on the run and delivering accurate deep balls. The Colts, sitting with a surplus of quarterback talent behind Anthony Richardson, could consider a trade that includes a fourth‑round pick and a future defensive back. Acquiring Pennington would give New York a young, high‑upside arm who could develop alongside Winston, creating a tandem that could be leveraged in future seasons.

While the Giants’ front office remains hopeful that Winston can find consistency, the looming trade deadline forces a realistic assessment of the team’s trajectory this year. The potential acquisitions each present distinct advantages—mobility, experience, developmental upside, or a blend of both—and each aligns with the franchise’s broader strategy of rebuilding while staying competitive enough to attract free agents. If New York can secure a trade that bolsters its quarterback depth without mortgaging the future, the Giants could stabilize their offense and lay groundwork for a more promising 2027 campaign. The coming weeks will reveal whether the organization opts for a quick fix or continues to gamble on its current roster, but one thing is clear: the quarterback position will dominate the Giants’ offseason narrative.
